# rosettacommons/rosettafoldsparkPowered by Gemini

# rosettacommons/rosettafoldsparkPowered by Gemini

Updated onJul 25, 2026Commit[`fcf9125`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/tree/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5)Gemini can make mistakes, so double\-check it\.![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This software repository implements a deep learning framework for predicting protein three\-dimensional structures and interactions\. It converts raw biological data into numerical representations, refines these representations through iterative processes, and translates predicted inter\-residue geometries into 3D models\. The framework also refines initial structures and assesses prediction quality\.

 The primary function of this repository involves a deep learning pipeline for protein structure prediction, detailed in [Protein Structure Prediction Core](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core)\. This core process includes:

 - [Feature Embedding and Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-feature-embedding-and-processing), which transforms raw biological data, such as amino acid sequences and Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), into high\-dimensional numerical features\.
- [Iterative Representation Refinement Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-iterative-representation-refinement-mechanisms), which enhance these features using attention\-based modules\.
- [Inter\-Residue Geometry Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-inter-residue-geometry-prediction), which determines inter\-residue distances and orientations from the refined features\.
- [Differentiable Folding and Initial 3D Structure Generation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-differentiable-folding-and-initial-3d-structure-generation), converting geometric predictions into 3D protein structures\.
- [SE\(3\)\-Equivariant Structural Refinement](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-se3-equivariant-structural-refinement), which refines the generated 3D structures using symmetry\-preserving neural networks\.
- [Transformer Components and Attention Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-transformer-components-and-attention-mechanisms), which are used throughout the pipeline to integrate information across different representations\. These components are assembled into [Integrated Model Architectures and Prediction Workflows](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-integrated-model-architectures-and-prediction-workflows) for end\-to\-end structure predictions\.

 Prior to prediction, [Input Data Preparation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#input-data-preparation) handles the generation of Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) and secondary structure predictions from raw sequences\. This includes specialized processes for [Paired MSA Generation for Protein Complexes](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#input-data-preparation-paired-msa-generation-for-protein-complexes)\.

 After initial structure prediction, further steps involve [Iterative Structure Refinement and Folding](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#iterative-structure-refinement-and-folding) using PyRosetta, which applies physics\-based minimization and relaxation protocols\. The framework also includes methods for [Protein Structure Error Prediction and Model Selection](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-error-prediction-and-model-selection) to evaluate model quality and choose diverse, high\-confidence structures\.

 The entire system leverages specialized neural network architectures that preserve 3D symmetries, detailed in [Equivariant Neural Network Components](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components)\. These components include [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) data structures for feature organization and [README\.md?plain=1 L92](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L92)\-equivariant graph neural networks for processing 3D data\. General [Machine Learning Utilities](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#machine-learning-utilities) support graph manipulation, experiment logging, and performance profiling\.## Protein Structure Prediction Core

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This section introduces the deep learning framework for predicting protein structure and interactions, which is the primary function of this repository\. It includes methods for converting biological data into numerical representations, refining these representations, predicting inter\-residue geometry \(distances and orientations\), and converting these predictions into 3D structures through a differentiable folding process\. The framework also encompasses initial iterative structural refinement steps\.

 The process begins with [Feature Embedding and Processing](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-feature-embedding-and-processing), where input data such as amino acid sequences, Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), and structural templates are transformed into high\-dimensional numerical features\. These features are then iteratively refined through various attention\-based modules, detailed in [Iterative Representation Refinement Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-iterative-representation-refinement-mechanisms), which propagate information within and between MSA and residue\-pair representations\.

 From these refined representations, the system predicts the full inter\-residue geometry, including distances and orientations \(omega, theta, and phi angles\), as described in [Inter\-Residue Geometry Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-inter-residue-geometry-prediction)\. These geometric predictions are then used by a differentiable folding algorithm to generate initial 3D protein structures, outlined in [Differentiable Folding and Initial 3D Structure Generation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-differentiable-folding-and-initial-3d-structure-generation)\.

 The generated 3D structures undergo further refinement using SE\(3\)\-equivariant networks, as explained in [SE\(3\)\-Equivariant Structural Refinement](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-se3-equivariant-structural-refinement)\. This ensures that the refinement process respects the fundamental symmetries of 3D space\. The system extensively uses Transformer components and various attention mechanisms, which are detailed in [Transformer Components and Attention Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-transformer-components-and-attention-mechanisms)\.

 Finally, these deep learning modules are integrated into comprehensive model architectures for end\-to\-end protein structure prediction, including specific prediction workflows for complexes and single chains\. More information on these integrated workflows can be found in [Integrated Model Architectures and Prediction Workflows](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-integrated-model-architectures-and-prediction-workflows)\.### Feature Embedding and Processing

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The initial step in protein structure prediction involves transforming raw biological data into numerical representations suitable for deep learning models\. This process, referred to as feature embedding, converts amino acid sequences, Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), and structural templates into high\-dimensional numerical vectors\.

 For sequence information, one\-dimensional sinusoidal positional encoding is used to capture the relative position of amino acids within a sequence\. This type of encoding is beneficial as it can generalize to varying sequence lengths\. Multiple Sequence Alignments are processed by embedding each amino acid and integrating positional and query\-specific information, where the query sequence \(the target protein\) is differentiated from other sequences in the alignment\. This is handled by modules in [`network/Embeddings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py) such as [Embeddings\.py L12](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py#L12), [Embeddings\.py L57](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py#L57), and [Embeddings\.py L69](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py#L69)\.

 Two\-dimensional pairwise features are created to represent interactions between residues\. These embeddings incorporate information from individual residue embeddings, their sequence separation, and optionally, structural template features\. The [Embeddings\.py L123](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py#L123) and [Embeddings\.py L152](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py#L152) modules in [`network/Embeddings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py) are responsible for generating these pairwise representations, with and without template data, respectively\. Two\-dimensional positional encoding, implemented by [Embeddings\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py#L33), is applied to these pairwise features to account for their spatial relationships\.

 Structural templates, when available, contribute additional features\. These templates, derived from existing protein structures, are processed by extracting one\-dimensional and two\-dimensional features\. An attention mechanism is applied along the template dimension to refine these features, and they are then combined into a weighted sum, as seen in the [Embeddings\.py L82](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py#L82) module in [`network/Embeddings.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Embeddings.py)\. The parsing of these various data types, such as A3M files for MSAs and PDB files for structural data, is managed by utilities within [`network/parsers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/parsers.py) and the [README\.md?plain=1 L52](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L52) module in [`network/ffindex.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/ffindex.py) which handles efficient retrieval from structural databases\. The gathered sequence and template data are then converted into the necessary tensor formats for processing by the deep learning model\.### Iterative Representation Refinement Mechanisms

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The iterative refinement of embedded Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) and residue\-pair features is a core mechanism for enhancing representations within the protein structure prediction pipeline\. This process employs attention\-based modules to integrate and propagate information both within and between these representations, thereby enriching the model's understanding of protein structure\.

 The modules facilitating this iterative refinement are primarily defined in [`network/Attention_module_w_str.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py) and [`network_2track/Attention_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network_2track/Attention_module.py)\. These components are inspired by architectures like AlphaFold2, systematically updating MSA and pair representations\.

 Key components include:

 - **[Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L149](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L149)**: Refines MSA features by applying attention mechanisms along the residue and sequence dimensions\. This allows information to be shared across different sequences in the alignment and along the length of each sequence, improving the representation of evolutionary conservation and variability\.
- **[Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L98](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L98)**: Generates and updates residue\-pair features using information derived from MSA features\. This module extracts co\-evolutionary signals and combines them with existing pair features, enhancing the model's understanding of inter\-residue relationships\.
- **[Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L178](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L178)**: Integrates information from refined residue\-pair features back into the MSA features\. This cross\-attention mechanism allows insights from pairwise residue interactions to inform and enrich the understanding of individual sequences within the MSA\.
- **[Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L191](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L191)**: Further refines residue\-pair features using axial attention, where attention is applied independently along each spatial dimension\. This helps capture intricate patterns in the 2D contact map representation\.

 These modules are orchestrated within [Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L288](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L288) and [Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L325](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L325) classes, which represent single iterations of this refinement process\. The [Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L410](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L410) in [`network/Attention_module_w_str.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py) manages the overall flow, applying a series of these blocks to progressively enhance the MSA and pair features\. The process can also include an initial structure prediction using [InitStrGenerator\.py L70](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/InitStrGenerator.py#L70) and subsequent structural updates via [Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L203](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L203) and [Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L253](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L253) \(see [Differentiable Folding and Initial 3D Structure Generation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-differentiable-folding-and-initial-3d-structure-generation)\)\. These structural updates, in turn, feed back into refining the MSA features\.

 The use of different attention mechanisms, including standard multi\-head attention and efficient linear attention variants like Performer \(see [Transformer Components and Attention Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-transformer-components-and-attention-mechanisms)\), contributes to the model's ability to process long sequences and complex alignments effectively\. This iterative and interconnected refinement cycle is fundamental to deriving high\-quality geometric predictions\.### Inter\-Residue Geometry Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Inter\-residue geometry prediction involves determining the spatial relationships between amino acid residues within a protein\. This task translates refined feature representations from upstream modules into quantifiable geometric data, specifically inter\-residue distances and orientation angles \(omega, theta, and phi\)\. These predictions are critical for subsequently reconstructing the protein's 3D structure\.

 The process is primarily handled by the [DistancePredictor\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/DistancePredictor.py#L9) class, found in [`network/DistancePredictor.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/DistancePredictor.py) and [`network_2track/DistancePredictor.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network_2track/DistancePredictor.py)\. This component takes the refined pairwise residue features as input\. It employs multiple 2D residual networks to predict distributions over discrete bins for each geometric parameter\. For example, distances and angles are typically binned into a predefined number of categories \(e\.g\., 37 bins for distance, omega, and theta, and 19 for phi\)\. This framing as a classification problem allows the model to output probabilities for each bin\.

 A notable aspect of this prediction is the treatment of symmetry\. Distances and omega angles between two residues are inherently symmetric, meaning the relationship from residue A to B is the same as from B to A\. To reflect this, the input features for distance and omega prediction are explicitly symmetrized before being processed by their respective residual networks\. In contrast, theta and phi angles, which describe local orientations, are directional and thus do not undergo symmetrization\.

 The geometric calculations that underpin the creation of these binned maps from actual 3D coordinates are described in [Differentiable Folding and Initial 3D Structure Generation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-differentiable-folding-and-initial-3d-structure-generation) and implemented in functions such as [kinematics\.py L80](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/kinematics.py#L80) and [kinematics\.py L157](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/kinematics.py#L157) within [`network/kinematics.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/kinematics.py)\. These functions are crucial for generating the ground truth data used to train the [DistancePredictor\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/DistancePredictor.py#L9)\. The predictions from the [DistancePredictor\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/DistancePredictor.py#L9) are then used by the [Differentiable Folding and Initial 3D Structure Generation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-differentiable-folding-and-initial-3d-structure-generation) module to convert these geometric restraints into an initial 3D structure\.### Differentiable Folding and Initial 3D Structure Generation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The generation of initial 3D protein structures and their refinement relies on a differentiable folding algorithm that translates predicted inter\-residue geometries into physical coordinates\. This process begins with the [Refine\_module\.py L5](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L5) module, which takes refined protein features and predicts initial C\-alpha or N, C\-alpha, C coordinates\. This initial structure prediction is conducted by the [InitStrGenerator\.py L70](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/InitStrGenerator.py#L70) in [`network/InitStrGenerator.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/InitStrGenerator.py), using a graph transformer architecture to process sequence and Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) features\. The network uses [InitStrGenerator\.py L46](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/InitStrGenerator.py#L46) instances, which are graph neural network blocks, to facilitate message passing and refine the nodal features representing the protein residues\. It also incorporates signed sequence separation to capture local structural context, building a graph where edges connect sequentially adjacent residues\.

 The predicted 3D coordinates then undergo iterative refinement, managed by the [Refine\_module\.py L115](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L115) in [`network/Refine_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py)\. This module orchestrates a series of refinement steps using SE\(3\)\-equivariant transformers\. The [Refine\_module\.py L14](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L14) within this module first establishes the initial atomic coordinates and a latent state vector from the protein's sequence and features\. Subsequently, a [Refine\_module\.py L62](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L62) iteratively updates these coordinates and states\. This iterative process uses SE\(3\)\-equivariant transformations, which maintain geometric symmetries, to refine the structural predictions\. To enhance robustness, the [Refine\_module\.py L115](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L115) incorporates data augmentation by mirroring structures, effectively doubling the batch size and ensuring consistency regardless of orientation\. The refinement continues until a stable local distance difference test \(LDDT\) score, indicating structural quality, is achieved or a maximum number of iterations is reached\.

 The [trFold\.py L83](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L83) algorithm further refines the predicted structures by minimizing an energy function based on the predicted inter\-residue distance and orientation maps\. This algorithm, implemented in [`network/trFold.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py) and utilized by the [predict\_e2e\.py L89](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/predict_e2e.py#L89) class in [`network/predict_complex.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/predict_complex.py), refines protein 3D structures from predicted geometric restraints\. The [trFold\.py L83](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L83) class contains methods for perturbing initial coordinates \([trFold\.py L5](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L5)\), converting quaternions to rotation matrices \([trFold\.py L12](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L12)\), and calculating geometric features like C\-beta coordinates \([trFold\.py L24](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L24)\), angles \([trFold\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L33)\), and dihedrals \([trFold\.py L55](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L55)\)\. Energy evaluation within [trFold\.py L83](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L83) is guided by Akima splines, which provide continuous potential energy functions from binned distance and orientation predictions\. These splines convert the predicted probability distributions for inter\-residue distances and angles into smooth, differentiable energy terms, enabling gradient\-based optimization during folding\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L69](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L69) script orchestrates the use of [trFold\.py L83](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L83) with specific [predict\_e2e\.py L68](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/predict_e2e.py#L68) that define smoothing kernels, distance cutoffs, angular step sizes, and clash penalties, guiding the minimization process\.

 The overall model architectures that integrate these components for end\-to\-end protein structure prediction are detailed in [Integrated Model Architectures and Prediction Workflows](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-integrated-model-architectures-and-prediction-workflows)\. The inter\-residue geometry predictions that drive this folding process are produced by the [DistancePredictor\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/DistancePredictor.py#L9) as described in [Inter\-Residue Geometry Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-inter-residue-geometry-prediction)\. The SE\(3\)\-equivariant networks employed in the refinement stages are discussed in [SE\(3\)\-Equivariant Structural Refinement](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-se3-equivariant-structural-refinement) and [Equivariant Neural Network Components](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components)\.### SE\(3\)\-Equivariant Structural Refinement

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Predicted 3D protein structures undergo an iterative refinement process that utilizes SE\(3\)\-equivariant networks\. This approach ensures that the refinement respects the fundamental symmetries of 3D space, which include rotation and translation\. The refinement process begins after the generation of initial 3D coordinates and an associated state representation by a module like [Refine\_module\.py L14](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L14) in [`network/Refine_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py)\. These initial coordinates are then refined iteratively by a [Refine\_module\.py L62](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L62), which employs an SE\(3\)\-equivariant transformer\.

 The [Refine\_module\.py L62](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L62) processes multiple sequence alignment \(MSA\) features, residue\-pair features, the current 3D coordinates, and an associated latent state\. It constructs a graph using these features and then applies an [SE3\_network\.py L54](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/SE3_network.py#L54) to predict coordinate shifts\. These predicted shifts are then used to update the atomic coordinates, leading to a refined structure and an updated latent state\. This iterative refinement continues for a set number of steps, monitoring predicted quality scores, such as lDDT, to select the most refined structure\. The overall process is orchestrated by the [Refine\_module\.py L115](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L115) in [`network/Refine_module.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py), which also incorporates data augmentation by mirroring structures to enhance robustness\.

 The underlying SE\(3\) equivariance is critical for handling 3D geometric data\. For more details on the specific components, refer to [Equivariant Neural Network Components](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components)\.### Transformer Components and Attention Mechanisms

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The core prediction pipeline extensively utilizes Transformer\-based architectures, primarily implemented within [`network/Transformer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py) and [`network/performer_pytorch.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/performer_pytorch.py), to process and refine protein representations\. These components facilitate various forms of attention mechanisms and encoder blocks critical for integrating information across multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\) and residue\-pair features\.

 Standard multi\-head attention is provided by the [Transformer\.py L43](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L43) module within [`network/Transformer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py)\. This mechanism allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions\. For scenarios requiring specific handling of input dimensions, such as MSAs, specialized attention variants are employed\. [Transformer\.py L84](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L84) and [Transformer\.py L157](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L157) \(which incorporates a [Transformer\.py L130](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L130) module to dynamically weight MSA sequences\) are designed to efficiently handle multiple sequences in an alignment by tying or softly tying attention computations\. [Transformer\.py L211](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L211) and [Transformer\.py L233](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L233) offer mechanisms where an attention map is derived from one representation \(e\.g\., residue\-pair features\) and applied to another \(e\.g\., MSA features\), enabling cross\-representation information flow\.

 Encoder blocks serve as foundational structures that stack these attention mechanisms with feed\-forward networks, often incorporating residual connections and layer normalization\. The [Transformer\.py L267](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L267) in [`network/Transformer.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py) represents a general\-purpose Transformer encoder block\. [Transformer\.py L312](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L312) is specifically designed for multi\-dimensional inputs, performing attention independently along different axes, which is beneficial for processing features that have both sequence length and multiple sequence dimensions\. [Transformer\.py L394](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Transformer.py#L394) facilitates cross\-attention between different types of representations, allowing, for instance, MSA features to interact with residue\-pair features\.

 To address computational efficiency, particularly with long sequences, the framework integrates efficient linear attention mechanisms inspired by Performer, implemented in [`network/performer_pytorch.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/performer_pytorch.py)\. The [performer\_pytorch\.py L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/performer_pytorch.py#L119) module computes attention using random feature maps, avoiding the explicit quadratic complexity of full attention matrices\. This is integrated into the [performer\_pytorch\.py L210](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/performer_pytorch.py#L210) module, which offers a scalable multi\-head self\-attention implementation, featuring techniques like periodic redrawing of projection matrices and batched processing for large inputs to manage memory\. These efficient attention mechanisms are crucial for handling the extensive sequence lengths often encountered in protein structure prediction problems\.

 These diverse attention mechanisms and encoder blocks are then integrated into larger model architectures such as [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L8) and [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L61)\. See [Integrated Model Architectures and Prediction Workflows](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-integrated-model-architectures-and-prediction-workflows) for more details\.### Integrated Model Architectures and Prediction Workflows

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The RoseTTAFold repository integrates various deep learning modules into comprehensive architectures for protein structure prediction, enabling end\-to\-end workflows for single chains, protein complexes, and PyRosetta\-compatible outputs\. The primary architectures, [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L8) and [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L61), orchestrate the entire prediction pipeline, from initial feature embedding to final 3D structure generation and refinement\.

 The [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L8), defined in [`network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py), is the core component that processes input sequences, multiple sequence alignments \(MSAs\), and optional structural templates\. It manages the feature embedding process, which converts raw biological data into numerical representations, and then channels these through an [Attention\_module\_w\_str\.py L410](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Attention_module_w_str.py#L410)\. This extractor refines MSA and residue\-pair features through multiple iterations, predicting initial 3D coordinates and local distance difference test \(LDDT\) scores\. Finally, a [DistancePredictor\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/DistancePredictor.py#L9) takes the refined pair features to predict inter\-residue distances and orientations, crucial for defining the protein's 6D coordinates\.

 Extending this core functionality, the [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L61), also found in [`network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py), incorporates a [Refine\_module\.py L115](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/Refine_module.py#L115) for iterative structural refinement\. This allows for an end\-to\-end differentiable pipeline, where initial predictions are continuously improved to yield more accurate 3D protein structures\. This module supports a "refine\-only" mode, allowing for targeted refinement of existing structural predictions\.

 For specific prediction tasks, dedicated scripts integrate these models:

 - Single\-chain protein structure prediction is handled by [`network/predict_e2e.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/predict_e2e.py), which utilizes [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L61) to generate refined PDB structures directly\.
- For protein complexes, [`network/predict_complex.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/predict_complex.py) employs [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L61](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L61) and a cropping strategy for larger sequences to predict complex structures\. The input for complex modeling often involves paired MSAs, as detailed in [Paired MSA Generation for Protein Complexes](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#input-data-preparation-paired-msa-generation-for-protein-complexes)\.
- Integration with PyRosetta for further physics\-based refinement is facilitated by [`network/predict_pyRosetta.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/predict_pyRosetta.py)\. This script uses [RoseTTAFoldModel\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/RoseTTAFoldModel.py#L8) to predict distance and orientation parameters, which are then fed into PyRosetta\-based folding protocols described in [Iterative Structure Refinement and Folding](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#iterative-structure-refinement-and-folding)\.

 A faster 2\-track version for protein\-protein interaction \(PPI\) screening is available through [`network_2track/predict_msa.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network_2track/predict_msa.py), which predicts inter\-chain contact probabilities using the [TrunkModel\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network_2track/TrunkModel.py#L8) architecture\. This module, defined in [`network_2track/TrunkModel.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network_2track/TrunkModel.py), processes sequence, MSA, and template data to iteratively refine features and predict inter\-residue distance distributions\.

 The overall prediction workflows are orchestrated by shell scripts such as [`run_e2e_ver.sh`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/run_e2e_ver.sh) and [`run_pyrosetta_ver.sh`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/run_pyrosetta_ver.sh)\. These scripts manage the entire pipeline, from preparing input data like MSAs and secondary structures \(see [Input Data Preparation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#input-data-preparation)\) to executing the deep learning models and performing post\-prediction refinement and model selection \(as described in [Protein Structure Error Prediction and Model Selection](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-error-prediction-and-model-selection)\)\.## Input Data Preparation

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Input data preparation involves converting raw biological sequences into formats suitable for deep learning models, focusing on generating Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) for individual proteins and protein complexes, as well as producing secondary structure predictions\. These processed inputs are crucial for the subsequent stages of protein structure prediction\.

 For single proteins, the process of generating high\-quality MSAs involves iterative searches against sequence databases\. This typically uses tools like [README\.md?plain=1 L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L81) to perform exhaustive searches and [make\_msa\.sh L36](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_msa.sh#L36) to refine the results based on sequence identity and coverage, ensuring a sufficient number of diverse sequences are collected\. The script [`input_prep/make_msa.sh`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_msa.sh) orchestrates these steps, managing search iterations with varying E\-values and filtering criteria to optimize MSA quality\. Once an MSA is generated, secondary structure predictions can be derived\. This involves converting the MSA into a checkpoint file and profile matrix, which are then used by prediction tools like [run\_e2e\_ver\.sh L46](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/run_e2e_ver.sh#L46) and [make\_ss\.sh L19](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_ss.sh#L19) to generate and refine secondary structure and confidence scores\. The script [`input_prep/make_ss.sh`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_ss.sh) automates this sequence of operations, from checkpoint file generation to prediction refinement and output formatting\.

 When dealing with protein complexes, a specialized approach is used to create paired MSAs\. This involves taking individual MSAs for each protein in the complex and merging them by identifying interacting protein sequences\. The script [`example/complex_modeling/make_joint_MSA_bacterial.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/example/complex_modeling/make_joint_MSA_bacterial.py) facilitates this by parsing individual MSA files, extracting Uniprot IDs, converting these IDs into unique integer hashes, and then identifying interacting pairs based on the proximity of their hash values\. This allows for the creation of a combined MSA where sequences from potentially interacting partners are aligned together, which is vital for predicting complex structures\.### MSA Generation for Single Proteins

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The generation of high\-quality Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) for individual protein sequences is a foundational step in protein structure prediction\. This process involves iteratively searching sequence databases and subsequently filtering the results\. The script responsible for this is located at [`input_prep/make_msa.sh`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_msa.sh)\.

 The core mechanism for MSA generation relies on iterative [README\.md?plain=1 L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L81) searches\. This tool is configured to perform searches against specified sequence databases, with parameters controlling output suppression, E\-value thresholds, coverage, and resource allocation \(CPU and memory\)\. The search strategy involves iterating through different databases and varying E\-values to ensure comprehensive coverage\.

 Following each [README\.md?plain=1 L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L81) search, the generated A3M files are filtered using [make\_msa\.sh L36](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_msa.sh#L36)\. This filtering step is crucial for refining the MSA by applying criteria such as sequence identity and coverage\. The process checks if a sufficient number of sequences \(e\.g\., 2000 sequences with 90% identity and 75% coverage, or 4000 sequences with 90% identity and 50% coverage\) have been accumulated\. If these thresholds are met, the loops terminate, and the filtered MSA is saved\. If the criteria are not met, the iterative search continues, using the previously generated A3M file as input for the next [README\.md?plain=1 L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L81) run\. The final output is an A3M file containing the refined MSA, intended for downstream protein structure prediction tasks\.

 Environment variables such as [run\_e2e\_ver\.sh L16](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/run_e2e_ver.sh#L16) and [make\_ss\.sh L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_ss.sh#L3) are used to locate necessary tools and databases, contributing to the script's portability within a structured bioinformatics environment\. This systematic approach ensures the generation of robust MSAs, which are critical inputs for subsequent deep learning models\. For a broader understanding of input data preparation, refer to [Input Data Preparation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#input-data-preparation)\.### Secondary Structure Prediction from MSAs

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The process of secondary structure prediction transforms a Multiple Sequence Alignment \(MSA\) into predicted secondary structure elements \(e\.g\., alpha\-helices, beta\-sheets\) and associated confidence scores\. This is a critical intermediate step in protein structure prediction, providing 1D structural cues that guide subsequent 3D modeling\. The primary script coordinating this process is [`input_prep/make_ss.sh`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_ss.sh)\.

 The workflow begins by converting the input A3M MSA file into a CSBLAST checkpoint file using [make\_ss\.sh L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_ss.sh#L11)\. This checkpoint format is optimized for subsequent profile matrix generation\. Following this, [make\_ss\.sh L17](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_ss.sh#L17) creates a profile matrix, which encapsulates statistical information about the sequence conservation and variability within the MSA\. This matrix serves as input for [run\_e2e\_ver\.sh L46](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/run_e2e_ver.sh#L46), an external tool that performs the initial secondary structure prediction using a set of learned weights\. The predictions from [run\_e2e\_ver\.sh L46](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/run_e2e_ver.sh#L46) are then refined by [make\_ss\.sh L19](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/input_prep/make_ss.sh#L19), which can integrate additional data to produce a more accurate final prediction\. The predicted secondary structure and confidence scores are then formatted for downstream use\. This modular approach leverages established bioinformatics tools to generate a robust secondary structure prediction\. For details on how the initial MSAs are generated, refer to [MSA Generation for Single Proteins](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#input-data-preparation-msa-generation-for-single-proteins)\.### Paired MSA Generation for Protein Complexes

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

For modeling protein complexes, specialized Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\) are generated by pairing sequences from two individual a3m files\. This process, primarily managed by [`example/complex_modeling/make_joint_MSA_bacterial.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/example/complex_modeling/make_joint_MSA_bacterial.py), aims to identify and merge potentially interacting protein sequences\.

 The initial step involves parsing the two input a3m files, extracting protein sequences and associated metadata\. A crucial component of this process is the [make\_joint\_MSA\_bacterial\.py L41](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/example/complex_modeling/make_joint_MSA_bacterial.py#L41) function, which converts UniProt IDs into numerical hashes\. This conversion utilizes a specific padding, character\-to\-numerical mapping, and a weighted summation scheme that varies based on the starting character of the UniProt ID\. This hashing provides a robust, numerical representation of each protein for comparison\.

 Once the UniProt IDs are converted to hashes, the system identifies interacting pairs\. It looks for sequences where the absolute difference between their hash values is below a predefined threshold, suggesting a close relationship or potential interaction\. This heuristic helps in filtering for biologically relevant partners within the vast sequence space\.

 The final output is a [README\.md?plain=1 L69](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L69) file\. This file begins with the concatenated query sequences from the two input MSAs, representing the primary interaction being modeled\. Subsequently, for each identified interacting pair, their respective labels and sequences are concatenated and appended to this joint MSA\. This structured [README\.md?plain=1 L69](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L69) then serves as an input for downstream deep learning models in protein structure prediction [Protein Structure Prediction Core](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core), allowing them to analyze and predict the structure of protein complexes\.## Iterative Structure Refinement and Folding

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The iterative structure refinement and folding process uses PyRosetta to generate and refine protein 3D structures\. This involves multiple minimization and relaxation steps guided by predicted restraints, with configurable parameters set via command\-line arguments\. The core functionality is implemented in [`folding/RosettaTR.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py)\.

 The process begins by generating an initial [RosettaTR\.py L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L81) [RosettaTR\.py L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L119) from the protein sequence, resolving steric clashes, and setting backbone dihedrals\. Glycine residues are temporarily mutated to Alanine to enhance stability during initial refinement\. Predicted distance and orientation matrices are converted into PyRosetta constraint objects using continuous potential energy functions like [utils\.py L86](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L86), with optional Savitzky\-Golay filtering for smoothing\. This is handled by [utils\.py L12](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L12) and [utils\.py L297](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L297) functions in [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py)\.

 The refinement proceeds through iterative centroid minimization\. In multiple runs, the weights of various [RosettaTR\.py L49](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L49) terms are adjusted, and restraints are incrementally added based on residue separation\. Minimization is performed, and the pose with the lowest Cartesian score is selected\. After centroid refinement, Glycines are reverted from Alanines\.

 For full\-atom refinement, the [RosettaTR\.py L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L119) is converted to an [RosettaTR\.py L229](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L229) representation, and problematic regions are idealized using [RosettaTR\.py L233](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L233)\. If enabled, a multi\-round [README L29](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/README#L29) protocol is executed, as defined in [`folding/data/relax_round1.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round1.txt) and [`folding/data/relax_round2.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt)\. These protocols use [relax\_round2\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L3) operations with progressive weighting and step sizes in both torsional and Cartesian phases, employing [relax\_round2\.txt L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L7) to retain the best energy states\. Coordinate restraints can be added during this phase to prevent large structural deviations, as managed by [utils\.py L351](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L351) in [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py)\.

 The entire process is configured through command\-line arguments parsed by [arguments\.py L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/arguments.py#L3) in [`folding/arguments.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/arguments.py), allowing control over inputs, output paths, number of restarts, restraint probability cutoffs, minimization steps, and the inclusion of orientation restraints or FastRelax\.### Centroid Pose Generation and Initial Minimization

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The initial phase of protein structure refinement involves generating centroid protein poses and performing initial minimization steps to resolve steric clashes and establish a foundational 3D structure\. This process is orchestrated by [`folding/RosettaTR.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py)\.

 The process begins by creating an initial [RosettaTR\.py L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L81) [RosettaTR\.py L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L119) object from the protein sequence\. Backbone dihedral angles \(phi, psi, and omega\) are then assigned\. These dihedrals can either be initialized randomly by sampling from predefined common dihedral angle regions or set based on predictions if available, using functions like [utils\.py L230](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L230) or [utils\.py L215](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L215) from [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py)\. To ensure stability during the initial centroid refinement, glycine residues are temporarily mutated to alanine, as glycines' conformational flexibility can introduce complications at this stage\. After the refinement, they are reverted to glycines\.

 A critical early step is the resolution of steric clashes within the newly generated pose\. This is achieved using [utils\.py L290](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L290) from [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py), which applies a [RosettaTR\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L8) with a van der Waals score function to quickly alleviate unfavorable atomic overlaps\.

 Following clash resolution, the system enters an iterative centroid minimization process\. This involves multiple runs where a [RosettaTR\.py L49](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L49) is carefully adjusted\. The weights for various scoring terms, such as van der Waals and the terms related to predicted distance and orientation restraints, are incrementally modified\. Specifically, the van der Waals weight is gradually increased, while the restraint weights might be adjusted to guide the folding\. Predicted structural features, such as distance, omega, theta, and phi matrices, are converted into [README\.md?plain=1 L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L13) constraint objects using [utils\.py L12](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L12) from [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py)\. These constraints are applied incrementally, often based on residue separation, allowing the model to progressively incorporate more global structural information as the minimization proceeds\. Minimization itself is performed using [RosettaTR\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L8) and [RosettaTR\.py L116](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L116) to optimize the protein's conformation according to the current [RosettaTR\.py L49](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L49) and applied restraints\. After each run, the pose with the lowest Cartesian score is selected, aiming to converge towards a more stable and accurate intermediate structure\.### Full\-Atom Refinement with FastRelax Protocols

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Following initial centroid\-based refinement, the protein structure prediction pipeline transitions to a full\-atom representation for detailed energy optimization\. This transition is managed by [RosettaTR\.py L229](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L229) in [`folding/RosettaTR.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py), converting the [RosettaTR\.py L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L119) object from a computationally efficient [RosettaTR\.py L81](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L81) model to a more physically realistic [RosettaTR\.py L229](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L229) \(full\-atom\) representation\. Prior to full\-atom relaxation, problematic regions in the structure, identified by high [RosettaTR\.py L237](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L237) energies, are idealized using [RosettaTR\.py L233](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L233) to ensure geometric validity\.

 The core of full\-atom refinement is the application of multi\-round [README L29](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/README#L29) protocols, which are aggressive relaxation procedures designed to optimize protein conformations while respecting chemical and physical constraints\. These protocols are configured in text files like [`folding/data/relax_round1.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round1.txt) and [`folding/data/relax_round2.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt)\. The [README L29](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/README#L29) method employs [relax\_round2\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L3) operations, which iteratively combine side\-chain repacking and backbone/side\-chain minimization\. These operations are applied with progressively increasing weighting and varying step sizes, allowing for a gradual yet thorough exploration of conformational space\.

 The relaxation protocols in [`folding/data`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data) define sequences of [relax\_round2\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L3) steps\. For example, [`folding/data/relax_round1.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round1.txt) outlines a two\-phase relaxation:

 - A [RosettaTR\.py L289](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L289) phase, where four [relax\_round2\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L3) steps are executed with increasing influence and varying step sizes, primarily optimizing torsional degrees of freedom\.
- A [trFold\.py L35](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L35) phase, performing similar [relax\_round2\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L3) steps to refine the structure in Cartesian space\.

 The [`folding/data/relax_round2.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt) protocol focuses exclusively on [trFold\.py L35](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L35) relaxation, repeating a sequence of four [relax\_round2\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L3) operations, again with progressively increasing strength and decreasing minimization tolerance\. After each sequence of [relax\_round2\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L3) operations, [relax\_round2\.txt L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L7) is invoked, ensuring that only energetically favorable conformations are retained\.

 To prevent excessive structural deviation during these aggressive relaxation steps, coordinate restraints are applied\. The [utils\.py L351](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L351) function in [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py) generates and applies [utils\.py L357](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L357) objects to the C\-alpha atoms of the protein, effectively "pinning" them to their original positions within a defined tolerance\. This strategy, combined with the progressive nature of [relax\_round2\.txt L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L3) and the [relax\_round2\.txt L7](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/data/relax_round2.txt#L7) mechanism, facilitates comprehensive energy optimization while preserving the overall fold predicted by earlier stages\. The process is managed by [README L29](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/README#L29) from [RosettaTR\.py L296](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L296) within [`folding/RosettaTR.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py)\.### Restraint Generation and Application from Predictions

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Predicted distance and orientation matrices are converted into PyRosetta constraint objects to guide the protein folding process\. This conversion and application primarily occur within [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py), which is orchestrated by [`folding/RosettaTR.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py) during the iterative refinement of protein structures\.

 The [utils\.py L12](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L12) function in [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py) processes raw probability distributions for inter\-residue distances, omega, theta, and phi angles\. It transforms these probabilities into continuous potential energy functions using [utils\.py L86](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L86)\. This process involves defining [utils\.py L63](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L63) \(representing distances or angles\) and corresponding [representations\.py L228](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py#L228) values \(representing energy, derived from the negative logarithm of probabilities\), which are then used to construct spline functions\. For instance, distance restraints involve calculating background, attractive, and repulsive potentials\. Orientation restraints for omega, theta, and phi angles are similarly processed, often incorporating circular padding to handle periodic boundaries smoothly\. An optional Savitzky\-Golay filter \([utils\.py L83](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L83) from [utils\.py L4](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L4)\) can be applied to smooth these distributions, potentially reducing noise in the predicted restraints\. The function ultimately returns a dictionary containing lists of [README\.md?plain=1 L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L13) constraint objects, such as [utils\.py L89](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L89) for distances and [utils\.py L118](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L118) or [utils\.py L168](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L168) for orientation\.

 These generated constraints are then applied to a protein [RosettaTR\.py L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L119) object using the [utils\.py L297](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L297) function, also found in [`folding/utils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py)\. This function filters constraints based on residue separation and probability cutoffs, then collects them into a [utils\.py L342](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L342)\. A [utils\.py L346](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L346) then applies this set to the [utils\.py L215](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L215)\. Additionally, coordinate restraints can be added to C\-alpha atoms using [utils\.py L351](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L351) to prevent large structural deviations during refinement, particularly during the full\-atom relaxation stages\. The application of these restraints is integral to the [Iterative Structure Refinement and Folding](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#iterative-structure-refinement-and-folding) process, guiding the minimization and relaxation steps towards predicted structural conformations\.## Protein Structure Error Prediction and Model Selection

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protein structure error prediction and model selection involves evaluating the quality of predicted protein structures, identifying regions of potential error, and choosing a diverse set of high\-quality models from a larger pool\. The process begins with generating numerical feature representations of protein structures, which are then used as input for deep learning models\. These models predict per\-residue error, enabling assessment of local structural accuracy\. Following error prediction, models are clustered based on their structural similarity to identify distinct conformations\. From these clusters, representative models with the highest predicted quality are selected\.

 The initial step in this process is to featurize protein structures, converting raw biological data into numerical representations\. This involves extracting various geometric, energetic, and sequence\-based features\. For example, distance and energy maps capture inter\-residue relationships, while amino acid properties and sequence features provide one\-dimensional context\. Further features include 6D neighbor features that describe residue\-residue orientations and distances, and 3D neighbor features that discretize local atomic environments around residues\. These features are extracted using tools such as PyRosetta, as detailed in [Comprehensive Protein Featurization for Deep Learning](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-error-prediction-and-model-selection-comprehensive-protein-featurization-for-deep-learning)\.

 Once featurized, these representations serve as input to deep learning models designed to predict protein structure quality\. These models, which can include convolutional neural networks with residual blocks and self\-attention mechanisms, process the 1D, 2D, and 3D features to estimate local distance difference test \(lDDT\) scores, estograms \(estimated distance distributions\), and confidence masks\. These predictions indicate the expected accuracy at each residue position\. The architecture leverages components like [layers\.py L4](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/layers.py#L4) from [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/layers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/layers.py) and [resnet\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/resnet.py#L10) from [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/resnet.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/resnet.py) to capture complex patterns in protein structures and their quality\.

 After error prediction, the system selects a diverse set of high\-quality models from a collection of predicted structures\. This is achieved by first filtering models based on their global quality scores\. The top\-performing models are then clustered using techniques like agglomerative clustering, where structural similarity is measured using pairwise lDDT distances\. From each cluster, the model with the highest predicted quality score is chosen as a representative\. This approach ensures that the selected models not only exhibit high confidence but also represent a range of distinct structural possibilities, which is crucial for downstream experimental validation or further analysis\. The script [`DAN-msa/pick_final_models.div.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pick_final_models.div.py) orchestrates this selection process, including the calculation of per\-residue coordinate error \([pick\_final\_models\.div\.py L145](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pick_final_models.div.py#L145)\) for the chosen models\.

 The entire workflow, from featurization to prediction and model selection, is supported by various data processing utilities\. These include functions for amino acid conversions, static data lookups for BLOSUM62 scores and atom group classifications, and data loading mechanisms for preparing features and labels for deep learning\. The data processing utilities also handle transformations of features, such as non\-linear scaling of distance values, and apply techniques like label smoothing during training to improve model generalization\. Further details on these utilities can be found in [Data Processing and Utilities for Error Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-error-prediction-and-model-selection-data-processing-and-utilities-for-error-prediction)\.### Comprehensive Protein Featurization for Deep Learning

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Protein structures are converted into numerical features for consumption by deep learning models through a multi\-faceted featurization process\. This process begins by initializing the [README\.md?plain=1 L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L13) environment\. Various geometric and energetic properties are extracted from protein [RosettaTR\.py L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L119) objects\. For instance, distance and energy maps capture inter\-residue relationships; these include matrices of distances between specific atoms \(e\.g\., CB\-CB, CA\-CA, Tip\-Tip\) and various inter\-residue energy terms \(e\.g\., hydrogen bond energies, attractive/repulsive forces\)\.
