 Amino acid properties are also extracted, generating a feature vector for each residue that includes one\-hot encoded amino acid types, [dataProcessingUtils\.py L31](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/dataProcessingUtils.py#L31) values \(from [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/dataProcessingUtils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/dataProcessingUtils.py)\), normalized residue position, and Meiler features\.

 Neighbor features in 6D and 3D space are computed\. This involves calculating [RosettaTR\.py L35](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L35) distances, dihedrals, and angles between contacting residues for 6D features, using efficient neighbor searching algorithms\. For 3D features, non\-hydrogen atom coordinates are projected onto local reference frames of nearby [trFold\.py L24](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/trFold.py#L24) atoms and then discretized, using trilinear interpolation to create a sparse representation of local atomic environments\.

 Additionally, 1D sequence and structure features are extracted, such as the amino acid sequence, DSSP secondary structure information, backbone dihedral angles \([representations\.py L217](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py#L217), [utils\.py L176](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L176)\), and beta\-strand pairing\. Further processing includes bond lengths and angles, as well as one\-body energy terms, with transformations applied to some energy and geometric data to enhance signal representation for downstream models\. The entire featurization process is orchestrated by a [featurize\.py L607](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/featurize.py#L607) function in [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/featurize.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/featurize.py) that loads a [RosettaTR\.py L119](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/RosettaTR.py#L119), extracts all relevant features, and saves them into a compressed [run\_pyrosetta\_ver\.sh L109](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/run_pyrosetta_ver.sh#L109) file\. These features are then consumed by deep learning models for error prediction, as detailed in [Comprehensive Protein Featurization for Deep Learning](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-error-prediction-and-model-selection-comprehensive-protein-featurization-for-deep-learning)\.### Data Processing and Utilities for Error Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The error prediction pipeline relies on efficient data handling and transformation to convert raw biological data into machine learning\-ready features\. Key utilities facilitate amino acid conversions, load static data, manage feature sets, and prepare target labels\.

 Amino acid representations are managed through dictionaries in [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/conversion.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/conversion.py)\. These allow for conversions between 3\-letter, 1\-letter, and numerical codes, and map 3\-letter codes to "tip" atoms for structural considerations\. Complementary mappings, such as amino acid lists, numerical indices, and 1\-letter codes, are initialized in [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/dataProcessingUtils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/dataProcessingUtils.py)\. This file also loads static data, including the BLOSUM62 substitution matrix from [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/data/blosum62.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/data/blosum62.txt), which provides scores for amino acid substitutions\. Additionally, it processes atomic grouping information from [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/data/groups20.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/data/groups20.txt) and [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/data/coarse-group20.txt`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/data/coarse-group20.txt), categorizing atoms into chemical groups for simplified representations\.

 Data loading and preprocessing are handled by the [deepLearningUtils\.py L9](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py#L9) class in [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py)\. This class is responsible for loading various 1D and 2D protein features, along with target labels, from [run\_pyrosetta\_ver\.sh L109](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/run_pyrosetta_ver.sh#L109) files\. It filters proteins based on length and data availability, and shuffles samples for training\. During data retrieval, it extracts features such as angles, predicted secondary structure information, amino acid properties, residue\-residue orientations, contact maps, and predicted residue\-residue contacts\. It also includes functions to generate sequence separation features and to convert distance residuals into a discretized, one\-hot encoded estogram\.

 Distance\-related features undergo transformations via the [deepLearningUtils\.py L171](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py#L171) function in [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py), which applies a non\-linear [predict\.py L48](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/predict.py#L48) scaling to normalize distance distributions, making them more suitable for model input\. For target labels, [deepLearningUtils\.py L189](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py#L189) in the same file implements a location\-aware label smoothing technique\. This regularizes the model by distributing a small portion of the true label's probability to adjacent classes, which helps prevent overfitting and improves generalization\. The [deepLearningUtils\.py L206](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py#L206) function in [`DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/deepLearningUtils.py) supports dynamic selection and exclusion of feature types, allowing for flexible input configurations for deep learning models\. These processed features are then used by the deep learning models for [Protein Structure Error Prediction and Model Selection](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-error-prediction-and-model-selection)\.## Equivariant Neural Network Components

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Equivariant neural network components are designed to process 3D geometric data while respecting fundamental symmetries of 3D space, specifically SE\(3\) equivariance, which includes invariance to rotations and translations\. This is achieved by representing features in a way that transforms predictably under these operations and designing network layers that preserve these properties\. The architecture relies on specialized data structures for handling fiber data, which are collections of features grouped by their spherical harmonic degrees\.

 The foundational data structure for these components is the [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) object, defined in [`network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py)\. A [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) organizes features based on their spherical harmonic degree, which is an integer representing the order of the spherical harmonic\. This allows for principled manipulation and combination of features that have different rotational behaviors\. Utilities are provided to convert between structured fiber representations and flat tensor formats, enabling integration with standard neural network operations while maintaining the underlying geometric structure\.

 Graph neural network modules, implemented in [`network/equivariant_attention/modules.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py), leverage these fiber data structures\. These modules include SE\(3\)\-equivariant graph convolutional layers that perform message passing on graphs, ensuring that feature interactions respect 3D symmetries\. Attention mechanisms, such as multi\-headed self\-attention blocks, are also designed to be SE\(3\)\-equivariant, allowing for context\-aware feature integration without breaking the rotational and translational symmetries\. Non\-linearities and normalization techniques are applied in an equivariant manner, typically by operating on feature norms to preserve their intrinsic orientation\. Pooling operations are also tailored for graph\-level features, specifically for scalar and vector components\.

 Supporting these equivariant modules are utilities for 3D rotations and irreducible representations, located in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py)\. These utilities handle the generation of 3D rotation matrices using ZYZ Euler angles, composition of rotations, and computation of irreducible representations of the SO\(3\) group\. This is crucial for understanding how features transform under rotations\. Furthermore, basis transformation matrices are provided to convert between Cartesian and spherical representations of vectors and tensors, which is essential for consistent processing of 3D data\.

 The computation of spherical harmonics is a core aspect of representing rotation\-equivariant features\. The [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py) file provides functions for computing associated Legendre functions and tesseral \(real\) spherical harmonics\. An optimized class for spherical harmonics utilizes memoization to efficiently compute these functions, which is particularly useful when multiple harmonics are required for various degrees and orders\.

 Additional utilities in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py) support steerable CNN computations\. These include functions for determining the null space of matrices, which is vital for solving linear constraints in equivariant transformations, and converting Cartesian coordinates to spherical coordinates\. The pre\-computation of spherical harmonics coefficients and a specialized scalar activation module further enhance the functionality for building robust 3D equivariant neural networks\.

 To ensure efficient and reliable computation, a persistent and process\-safe caching mechanism is implemented in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/cache_file.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/cache_file.py)\. This mechanism uses a combination of in\-memory LRU cache and file\-system\-based storage for gzipped pickle files\. It incorporates mutexes and file locking to prevent race conditions when multiple processes access the cache concurrently, thereby maintaining data integrity and improving performance during development and execution\.### Fiber Data Structures and Operations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) data structure serves as a fundamental abstraction for handling feature representations within equivariant neural networks, particularly when processing 3D geometric data where features are characterized by spherical harmonic degrees\. Defined in [`network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py), a [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) object organizes collections of features based on their degree, which correlates with how they transform under 3D rotations\.

 A [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) is composed of a [README\.md?plain=1 L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/README.md?plain=1#L40) that details the multiplicities \(number of channels\) for each spherical harmonic degree\. This allows the system to manage heterogeneous feature sets, where, for instance, scalar features \(degree 0\) might coexist with vector features \(degree 1\) or higher\-order tensor features\. The [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) class facilitates operations such as initialization with specified degrees and channel counts, creating copies, and combining multiple [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) objects\. Combination methods like [fibers\.py L55](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L55) and [fibers\.py L66](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L66) merge feature structures, either by summing multiplicities for common degrees or by taking the maximum, providing flexibility in how different feature sets are integrated\.

 Beyond managing the structure of these feature collections, utilities are provided to convert between the structured [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) representation and flat [utils\_steerable\.py L202](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L202) representations\. Functions such as [fibers\.py L114](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L114) and [fibers\.py L132](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L132) enable the conversion of a flat tensor back into a degree\-indexed dictionary of tensors, and vice versa\. This conversion is crucial for interfacing the degree\-specific feature handling of equivariant networks with standard tensor operations\. Specialized conversion functions like [fibers\.py L145](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L145) and [fibers\.py L155](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L155) are also available\. [fibers\.py L145](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L145) concatenates degree\-specific tensors into a single tensor, while [fibers\.py L155](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L155) further reshapes these for use in multi\-head attention mechanisms, introducing an additional dimension to accommodate the different attention heads\. These utilities ensure that the sophisticated [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) representation can be seamlessly integrated into the PyTorch deep learning ecosystem while maintaining the necessary rotational equivariance properties\. For more details on the operations performed using these fibers, refer to [Equivariant Graph Neural Network Modules](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components-equivariant-graph-neural-network-modules)\.### Equivariant Graph Neural Network Modules

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This section focuses on the implementation of SE\(3\)\-equivariant graph neural network modules within the Deep Graph Library \(DGL\) framework\. These modules are designed to process 3D geometric data by ensuring that network operations respect fundamental symmetries, specifically invariance to rotations and translations in 3D space\.

 A core component is the computation of equivariant basis functions, which define how features of different spherical harmonic degrees interact under rotations\. This is handled by functions like [modules\.py L85](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L85) in [`network/equivariant_attention/modules.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py), which precompute the SE\(3\)\-equivariant weight basis and inter\-nodal distances for a given graph\.

 Graph convolution layers, such as [modules\.py L109](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L109) in [`network/equivariant_attention/modules.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py), perform message passing on graphs while maintaining equivariance\. These layers leverage [modules\.py L269](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L269), also found in [`network/equivariant_attention/modules.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py), to calculate weights between different input and output feature types \(spherical harmonic degrees\)\. [modules\.py L269](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L269) uses a [modules\.py L231](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L231) \(a small multilayer perceptron\) to generate radial weights based on edge features, which are then combined with the precomputed equivariant basis to form the convolution kernel\.

 Non\-linearities and normalization are provided by modules like [modules\.py L340](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L340) and [modules\.py L457](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L457) in [`network/equivariant_attention/modules.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py)\. These modules apply non\-linear transformations or normalization to the norms of features while preserving their phase \(orientation\), a crucial aspect for maintaining equivariance\.

 For integrating attention mechanisms, the [modules\.py L650](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L650) module in [`network/equivariant_attention/modules.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py) implements a multi\-headed self\-attention block for SE\(3\)\-equivariant features on graphs\. It computes attention weights based on key and query embeddings and applies them to value embeddings, all within an equivariant framework\. Further details on the attention mechanisms can be found in [Transformer Components and Attention Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#protein-structure-prediction-core-transformer-components-and-attention-mechanisms)\.

 Residual and skip connections are incorporated using modules like [modules\.py L734](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L734) in [`network/equivariant_attention/modules.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py), which integrates attention with residual pathways\. Utility modules like [modules\.py L805](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L805) and [modules\.py L844](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L844) in the same file facilitate combining feature dictionaries\. The features themselves are organized using a [fibers\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/fibers.py#L13) object, as described in [Fiber Data Structures and Operations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components-fiber-data-structures-and-operations)\.

 The implementation relies heavily on DGL's message passing paradigm, utilizing functions such as [modules\.py L226](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L226) and user\-defined functions \(UDFs\) to define custom message computations for efficient graph operations\.### 3D Rotations and Irreducible Representations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [modules\.py L10](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/modules.py#L10) sub\-directory provides foundational utilities for generating and manipulating 3D rotations, specifically using ZYZ Euler angles\. This includes functions to construct rotation matrices for the Z and Y axes, as well as a composite ZYZ Euler angle rotation matrix\. It also allows for the conversion of 3D Cartesian points to Euler angles, which is useful for relating spatial coordinates to orientation\. Rotations can be composed, meaning two sequential rotations can be combined into a single equivalent rotation, verifying the group property of rotations\.

 A key aspect of this module is its handling of irreducible representations \(irreps\) of the SO\(3\) group\. Irreps are fundamental for describing how objects transform under rotation in a way that respects their inherent symmetries\. The [SO3\.py L77](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py#L77) function calculates the irreducible representation matrix for a given order and ZYZ Euler angles\. This calculation relies on an external [SO3\.py L82](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py#L82) function, which performs the complex mathematical operation of computing Wigner D\-matrices\.

 Furthermore, the module includes utilities for basis transformations\. These allow for the conversion of vector and tensor representations between Cartesian coordinates \(e\.g\., [featurize\.py L192](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/DAN-msa/pyErrorPred/featurize.py#L192)\) and their spherical harmonic components\. For instance, [SO3\.py L146](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py#L146) provides a matrix to convert a Cartesian vector into a form that transforms under the l=1 irrep\. Similarly, [SO3\.py L167](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py#L167) offers matrices to decompose a 3x3 tensor into its l=0, l=1, and l=2 irreducible components\. These transformations are critical for ensuring that features correctly transform under rotation when using equivariant neural networks, as discussed in [Equivariant Graph Neural Network Modules](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components-equivariant-graph-neural-network-modules)\.

 The [SO3\.py L12](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py#L12) context manager is used to temporarily set the default [util\.py L4](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/util.py#L4) data type, often to [SO3\.py L152](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py#L152), to ensure numerical precision during internal computations, particularly for complex matrix operations\.### Spherical Harmonics Computation

```
sph_har = SphericalHarmonics()
# Define angles (in radians)
theta = torch.tensor([0.5, 1.0])
phi = torch.tensor([0.1, 0.2])

# Get spherical harmonics for degree l=0
# All m values are computed and stacked: [-l, ..., l]
Y_l0 = sph_har.get(l=0, theta=theta, phi=phi)
print(f"Spherical harmonics for l=0:\n{Y_l0}")

# Get spherical harmonics for degree l=1
# This implicitly uses the memoized results for l=0
Y_l1 = sph_har.get(l=1, theta=theta, phi=phi, refresh=False)
print(f"Spherical harmonics for l=1:\n{Y_l1}")

# Demonstrate memoization by directly accessing a previously computed value
# This will not recompute lpmv(0, 0, ...)
l0_m0_val = sph_har.lpmv(l=0, m=0, x=torch.cos(theta))
print(f"Memoized lpmv(0, 0, x):\n{l0_m0_val}")

# To clear the memoization cache
sph_har.clear()
```

The computation of spherical harmonics is fundamental for representing 3D spatial information in a rotationally equivariant manner within the deep learning models\. This repository provides implementations for calculating associated Legendre functions and tesseral \(real\) spherical harmonics, which are crucial for constructing features that transform predictably under 3D rotations\.

 The functions for computing these mathematical components are primarily located in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py)\. This file offers both standalone functions and an optimized [representations\.py L103](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py#L103) class\. The associated Legendre functions, including the Condon\-Shortley phase, are computed using recursive relations\. These Legendre functions are then combined with trigonometric functions \(cosine and sine\) to form tesseral spherical harmonics, accounting for their angular dependence\. Helper functions such as [representations\.py L8](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py#L8) and [representations\.py L24](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py#L24) support these calculations\.

 A key optimization for efficiency is the [representations\.py L103](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py#L103) class, which employs memoization\. This means that previously computed associated Legendre function values are stored, significantly reducing redundant computations when multiple spherical harmonics are required for the same degree and order\. This is particularly beneficial when the system needs to retrieve all harmonics for a given degree, as it avoids recalculating intermediate values\. The [representations\.py L188](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py#L188) method of this class aggregates all tesseral spherical harmonics for a specified degree [README L21](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/README#L21)\.

 Further utilities in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py) wrap these spherical harmonic computations, allowing for efficient pre\-computation and storage of spherical harmonics coefficients\. These pre\-computed coefficients are then utilized by the network to manage various spherical harmonic orders, a process that can be further understood by examining the [Steerable CNN Utilities and Coordinate Transformations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components-steerable-cnn-utilities-and-coordinate-transformations) section\. This modular approach ensures that the potentially complex mathematical operations of spherical harmonics are handled efficiently and systematically throughout the deep learning architecture\.### Steerable CNN Utilities and Coordinate Transformations

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The repository provides specialized utilities designed to support the implementation of steerable Convolutional Neural Networks \(CNNs\), particularly for operations involving 3D geometric transformations and symmetries\. These utilities facilitate the handling of transformations between coordinate systems, the computation of spherical harmonics, and the robust determination of matrix null spaces\.

 A key aspect involves transforming 3D Cartesian coordinates into spherical coordinates \(radius, alpha, beta\)\. The functions [utils\_steerable\.py L71](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L71) and [utils\_steerable\.py L124](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L124) in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py) perform this conversion, defining [t000\_\.hhr L412](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/example/pyrosetta/t000_.hhr#L412) as the polar angle \(from 0 to pi\) and [utils\.py L45](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/folding/utils.py#L45) as the azimuthal angle\. This coordinate transformation is crucial for aligning data with the mathematical framework of spherical harmonics\.

 For efficient steerable operations, spherical harmonics coefficients are pre\-computed\. The [utils\_steerable\.py L271](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L271) function in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py) takes relative positional information and a maximum spherical harmonic order, then calculates and stores these coefficients\. This process leverages the [representations\.py L103](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/representations.py#L103) class described in [Spherical Harmonics Computation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components-spherical-harmonics-computation), which employs memoization for performance optimization\.

 Another utility involves computing the null space \(kernel\) of matrices, which is vital for solving linear constraints in equivariant networks\. Functions such as [utils\_steerable\.py L13](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L13) and [utils\_steerable\.py L29](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L29) in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py) utilize Singular Value Decomposition \([utils\_steerable\.py L22](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L22)\) to identify the null space, filtering singular values below a specified threshold for numerical stability\. This capability is used in [utils\_steerable\.py L37](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L37) to derive SO\(3\) transformation matrices, which are then cached using the mechanism detailed in [Persistent Caching Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components-persistent-caching-mechanisms) to avoid redundant computations\.

 The Kronecker product, implemented by the [SO3\.py L135](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/SO3.py#L135) function in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py), is also a component of these utilities, used in various matrix operations within the equivariant framework\. Additionally, a [utils\_steerable\.py L296](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py#L296) module in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/utils_steerable.py) applies activation functions to scalar fields, optionally incorporating learnable bias parameters\. These components collectively enable the construction and operation of steerable CNNs, ensuring that network operations respect 3D rotational symmetries\.### Persistent Caching Mechanisms

```
# Assume FileSystemMutex and cached_dirpklgz are defined as in source.

# Example usage of FileSystemMutex for a protected operation
mutex_file_path = "my_protected_resource.lock"
with FileSystemMutex(mutex_file_path):
    # This block is protected by the mutex.
    # Only one process can enter this block at a time.
    print(f"Process {os.getpid()} has acquired the lock.")
    # Simulate some protected work
    time.sleep(0.1)
    print(f"Process {os.getpid()} releasing the lock.")

@cached_dirpklgz(dirname="my_cache_dir")
def my_complex_function(arg1, arg2):
    """
    A function that takes time to compute and whose results we want to cache.
    The decorator handles caching to 'my_cache_dir' and uses FileSystemMutex
    internally to ensure safe file access across processes.
    """
    print(f"Computing result for {arg1}, {arg2}...")
    time.sleep(0.5)  # Simulate expensive computation
    return f"Result for {arg1}-{arg2}"

# First call: computes and caches the result
result1 = my_complex_function("hello", 123)
print(f"Function call 1 result: {result1}")

# Second call with same arguments: retrieves from cache
result2 = my_complex_function("hello", 123)
print(f"Function call 2 result: {result2}")

# New arguments: computes and caches a new result
result3 = my_complex_function("world", 456)
print(f"Function call 3 result: {result3}")
```

A persistent and process\-safe caching mechanism, located in [`network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/cache_file.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/cache_file.py), leverages both in\-memory LRU cache and a file\-system based cache\. This system is implemented via the [cache\_file\.py L48](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/cache_file.py#L48) decorator, which stores function results as gzipped pickle files on disk\. Data integrity and prevention of race conditions during cache access are ensured by the [cache\_file\.py L12](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/cache_file.py#L12) class, which uses [cache\_file\.py L27](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/equivariant_attention/from_se3cnn/cache_file.py#L27) for mutual exclusion across different processes\. This mechanism is crucial for operations, such as those discussed in [Steerable CNN Utilities and Coordinate Transformations](https://codewiki.google/github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold#equivariant-neural-network-components-steerable-cnn-utilities-and-coordinate-transformations), to avoid redundant computations, especially in environments with multiple concurrent processes\.## Machine Learning Utilities

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This section covers general utility functions for the machine learning aspects of the repository, including tools for graph data manipulation, logging, counting model parameters, tracking gradients, and conditional profiling to aid in model development and optimization\.

 Graph data manipulation is supported through utilities that handle [RoseTTAFold\-linux\.yml L106](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/RoseTTAFold-linux.yml#L106) graph objects\. These include functionalities for deep copying graphs, pickling graph data for storage, and updating relative positional information as edge data\. For instance, the [utils\_data\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_data.py#L11) class in [`network/utils/utils_data.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_data.py) facilitates saving and loading graph structures by converting node and edge attributes into NumPy arrays\.

 For managing training runs, a set of logging and monitoring utilities is provided\. These functions, found in [`network/utils/utils_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py), create structured log directories, count trainable parameters within PyTorch models, and capture detailed information about each training session, including Git commit IDs and command\-line arguments\. This ensures reproducibility and provides a comprehensive record of experiments\. Additionally, gradient norms can be tracked during the backward pass to monitor model stability\.

 To assist with performance analysis, a conditional profiling mechanism is available\. This mechanism, implemented in [`network/utils/utils_profiling.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_profiling.py), allows developers to instrument code with a [utils\_logging\.py L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py#L20) decorator\. When an external profiling library is active, it enables performance measurement; otherwise, it acts as a no\-operation, preventing errors without requiring code modification\.### Graph Data Manipulation Utilities

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Utilities are provided for manipulating and transforming graph data, specifically focusing on Deep Graph Library \(DGL\) graph objects\. These utilities facilitate common operations required for graph\-based machine learning models, such as deep copying graphs, efficient serialization \(pickling\), and updating relative positional information between nodes\.

 To support the persistence and transfer of graph structures, a [utils\_data\.py L11](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_data.py#L11) class in [`network/utils/utils_data.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_data.py) is available\. This class enables the serialization of DGL graph data by storing node and edge attributes as NumPy arrays, along with the source and destination indices for edges\. This design addresses the challenges of pickling complex DGL graph objects directly, providing a simplified representation that can be easily saved and loaded\.

 For scenarios requiring independent copies of graph data, the [utils\_data\.py L40](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_data.py#L40) function in [`network/utils/utils_data.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_data.py) creates deep copies of DGL graphs\. This is particularly useful when graph structures or their associated data need to be modified without affecting original instances, or when preparing batches of graphs for parallel processing\. The function handles both unbatched and batched graphs, ensuring all node and edge data are correctly duplicated\.

 Furthermore, [utils\_data\.py L59](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_data.py#L59) in [`network/utils/utils_data.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_data.py) calculates and integrates relative positional data into the graph's edge attributes\. This utility is crucial for models that rely on the spatial relationships between nodes, often observed in protein structure prediction where the distance or orientation between amino acid residues is a significant feature\. By computing the difference in absolute positions between connected nodes and storing this as edge data, the graph effectively captures the geometric context relevant for downstream predictions\.### Logging, Parameter Counting, and Gradient Tracking

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The repository incorporates utilities for managing experiment logs, determining model complexity, and monitoring training stability through gradient tracking\. A function within [`network/utils/utils_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py) facilitates the creation of structured log directories, automatically generating unique names based on timestamps or user\-defined inputs\. This setup ensures that various artifacts of a training run, such as model checkpoints and point cloud data, are organized consistently\.

 For reproducibility, a comprehensive [utils\_logging\.py L44](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py#L44) function, also found in [`network/utils/utils_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py), captures essential details of each experiment\. This includes the current Git commit hash, command\-line arguments used, and a [utils\_logging\.py L47](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py#L47) output, providing a precise record of the code state\. It also quantifies the model's complexity by reporting the total number of trainable parameters in PyTorch models, distinguishing between overall model parameters and those within specific encoder and decoder components\. This parameter count, implemented by [utils\_logging\.py L33](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py#L33) in [`network/utils/utils_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py), is crucial for understanding the computational demands and capacity of different model architectures\.

 To assess training stability and identify potential issues like vanishing or exploding gradients, the system includes a mechanism for tracking gradient norms\. The [utils\_logging\.py L101](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py#L101) function in [`network/utils/utils_logging.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py) registers a hook on specified tensors to record the L2 norm of their gradients during the backward pass\. These recorded norms are stored and can be averaged using [utils\_logging\.py L112](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py#L112), providing insights into how gradients behave across different parts of the network\. This allows developers to monitor and diagnose training pathologies, contributing to more robust model development\.### Conditional Profiling Mechanism

```
# In rosettafold/network/utils/utils_profiling.py
try:
    profile
except NameError:
    def profile(func):
        """
        A no-op decorator used when a global 'profile' object (e.g., from line_profiler)
        is not defined. It simply returns the original function.
        """
        return func

# Example usage within the codebase:

@profile
def my_function_to_profile(arg1, arg2):
    """
    This function will be decorated by the conditional 'profile' decorator.
    If a global profiler is present, it will apply profiling.
    Otherwise, this decorator acts as a no-op, and the function executes normally.
    """
    result = arg1 + arg2
    # ... more complex logic ...
    return result

# When 'profile' is not globally defined (as in the snippet above),
# @profile is equivalent to: my_function_to_profile = profile(my_function_to_profile)
# which, in this case, becomes: my_function_to_profile = my_function_to_profile
# The function's behavior is unchanged.
```

A conditional profiling decorator allows for selective performance profiling of code sections without requiring modifications to the code when profiling is not active\. This mechanism ensures that code can be instrumented with [utils\_logging\.py L20](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_logging.py#L20) decorators, but these decorators only perform profiling actions if a global profiler object is present\. If no such object is found, the decorator acts as a no\-op, passing through the decorated function unchanged\. This design avoids [utils\_profiling\.py L3](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_profiling.py#L3) exceptions that would otherwise occur if a profiling library's [utils\_profiling\.py L4](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_profiling.py#L4) object were referenced directly when the library is not loaded or active\. This functionality is implemented within the file [`network/utils/utils_profiling.py`](https://github.com/rosettacommons/rosettafold/blob/fcf9125c59e3dd84cf511dcb475ddd81a23613f5/network/utils/utils_profiling.py)\.
